title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 128
paragraphs: Such was the number of suitors. When they had arrived by the appointed day, Cleisthenes first asked them about their native countries and the genealogy of each, and then kept them for a year, testing continually their courage, character, upbringing, and temperament, both in his conversations with each of them individually and in their company as a group. He tested them by taking the younger ones out for athletic exercises, and, above all, at their daily meals together: for during all the time he kept them there, he did everything of the kind that could be done, and entertained them magnificently. It so happened that the ones who pleased him most were those who had come from Athens, and of these he preferred Hippocleides son of Tisander, both for his personal qualities and because he was connected by descent with the Cypselid family of Corinth.
